summary.headline: Tips Music Q2 FY27 revenue rose 35% YoY to INR120 crore and EBITDA margin hit 70.5%, with FY27 content spend guided at INR90-100 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR120 crore, up 35% YoY from INR89.2 crore, with operating EBITDA of INR84.64 crore (70.5% margin, up 25% YoY) and PAT of INR65.5 crore (54% margin, up 23%). H1 FY27 revenue was INR227 crore (up 28%) and H1 PAT INR109 crore (up 11%), with content cost front-loaded at INR71 crore in H1. Management said growth came from both new releases and catalogue, mainly volume-driven, and kept the full-year content guidance at INR90-100 crore. Revenue and PAT growth guidance was stated as 20%, with management saying it would exceed that without giving a specific number. The YouTube Shorts deal remains under negotiation.

financial_highlights.change: Q1 FY27 was 75%, implied Q2 about 71%

segments.name: Digital streaming
segments.commentary: Digital contributed 73% of H1 FY27 revenue; management guides digital share at 70-75% for the year. Subscription revenue is 10-15% of the digital pie.

segments.name: Non-digital
segments.commentary: Non-digital contributed the remaining share of revenue and grew alongside digital, per management. No separate figures were disclosed.

segments.name: Warner partnership
segments.commentary: Warner share of revenue is about 25-30% of H1 FY27 per management, and management said it increased YoY. The Warner deal renews in FY28.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 content spend maintained at INR90-100 crore, with H2 content lighter and mainly smaller films and non-film music.
Management said FY27 revenue and PAT growth would exceed the 20% guidance, but gave no specific figure; Kumar Taurani asked investors to treat it as 20%.
Management targets 5-6 films a year, of which 4-5 Hindi and 2-3 regional, and says content budget is about 20-22% of top line.
YouTube Shorts deal expected to be mostly completed in Q3 FY27, per Kumar Taurani; no value was quantified.
Per-stream YouTube rate expected to stay at about INR0.05 per stream, with no increase planned.
Buyback of INR44.44 crore completed; interim dividend of INR6.5 per share declared.
capex_capacity: No capex, capacity, utilisation or commissioning timelines were discussed on the call; the only capacity-type items were volume targets for releases.
Release volume: 73 songs released in Q2 FY27 (40 film, 33 non-film); management targets 5-6 films a year, of which 4-5 Hindi and 2-3 regional.
Content investment: FY27 content spend maintained at INR90-100 crore, with H1 at INR71 crore (front-loaded) and H2 described as lighter, mainly smaller films and non-film music.
Content budget guided at about 20-22% of top line; Kumar Taurani said bigger content deals could take it to 25-28%, which would hit profitability.
Management said the company is searching for a new CEO but has not found a suitable candidate yet.
demand_pricing: Growth was primarily volume-driven, per management; subscription price growth was described as healthy but marginal to growth.
Q2 growth was attributed to new releases and catalogue. 73 songs released in Q2 (40 film, 33 non-film). Catalogue track Aankhon Se Tune 2.0 has 66 million YouTube views.
Management estimates Tips holds 8-10% of industry revenue market share.
About 85% of revenue comes from content acquired more than three years ago and 15% from content acquired in the last three years.
Management said content cost inflation is driven by intense competition and high acquisition costs; it targets payback in 4-5 years.
Management said there are no major OTT renewals due in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of digital vs non-digital growth and the sustainability of 35% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Sushant Dalmia said growth came from new releases and catalogue across both digital and non-digital. Digital was 73% of H1 revenue and the growth was primarily volume-driven.

qa_highlights.question: Why did digital share fall from 75% in Q1 to about 71% in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said digital share is guided at 70-75%, declined to explain a 1-2 point move, and said profitability is unaffected because content and fixed costs are broadly fixed across segments.

qa_highlights.question: Is the upgraded guidance conservative given H1 growth of 28%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would stay conservative, with H2 potentially stronger during the festive season, and would exceed 20%. Kumar Taurani said to treat the guidance as 20% for now.

qa_highlights.question: Will content investment guidance change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management maintained INR90-100 crore for the full year. H1 spend was front-loaded and H2 will be lighter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did advertising/promotion spend rise in Q2 with no major release?
qa_highlights.answer: Sushant Dalmia said promotion is part of content cost and was driven by the front-loaded H1 releases, including Main Wapas Aaunga, released mid-June, whose promotions continued into Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Will the YouTube Shorts deal be concluded and how big will it be?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the deal is still under negotiation and is expected to be mostly completed in Q3 FY27, but gave no sizing.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Warner deal performing and when does it renew?
qa_highlights.answer: Warner's share is 25-30% of H1 revenue and rose YoY, per management. The deal renews in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the subscription contribution, and when is the paid subscription share rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Paid subscription is 10-15% of the digital pool. Management said higher per-stream rates from paid subscription are the main driver of future growth.

risks_watch: Full-year content guidance of INR90-100 crore is about 20-22% of top line, and management flagged that bigger content deals could push that share to 25-28%, which would hit profitability.
YouTube Shorts and Instagram Reels deal timing and value remain unquantified and have slipped by about 3-4 months.
Management said the Warner renewal in FY28 and the deal's terms will be key.
Management said it is searching for a new CEO without a named candidate.
Digital share moved from 75% in Q1 to about 71% in Q2, which management did not explain.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and catalogue performance, but cautious and non-committal on specifics: guidance was kept at 20% with no number given for the upgrade, and deal values, YouTube Shorts sizing and the Q2 digital mix shift were left unexplained.
key_quotes: It would be primarily volume-driven growth.
We would like to be conservative in our guidance.
It's better to under-promise and over-deliver.
We are absolutely clean, everything gets switched off.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue and PAT growth of 20%, said it would exceed that without a figure, and held content spend at INR90-100 crore; backing is vague, as growth was described as volume-driven from releases and catalogue with no capacity or contracts quantified.

mgmt.note: Management said it is searching for a new CEO but has not yet found a suitable candidate; no growth stance given.
